item.title: Transcript & Video: Lamont’s 2026 State Of The State Address
item.description: The full text of Gov. Ned Lamont's State of the State Address in Connecticut's House of Representatives on Wednesday.

item.title: Lamont Draws On ‘Connecticut Common Sense’ In State Of The State Address
item.description: Drawing from Thomas Paine’s 1776 pamphlets, Common Sense, and The American Crisis, Lamont delivered a 40-minute speech with few surprises, and a handful of controversial moments.

item.title: Trump Admin Too Harsh On Immigrants, 60% Of Voters Say In QPoll
item.description: Six in 10 voters think the Trump administration is being too harsh in its treatment of undocumented immigrants and more than half think Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem should be removed from office, according to a recent Quinnipiac University poll released Wednesday.

item.title: CT House Speaker Reprimands ‘Tomfoolery’ After Member Wears ICE-Related Message During State Of The State Address
item.description: “This is the historic House of Representatives,” the Hartford Democrat said as he opened the Feb. 5 session. “It’s not an elementary school, and I’m not a hallway monitor. I am the duly elected speaker of the house, and I was elected to enforce the rules of this chamber and I will do that.”

item.title: Lamont Budget Adjustments Draw Criticism From School And Hospital Groups, Among Others
item.description: The revised budget includes $12.5 million to fund universal free school breakfast and eliminate reduced-price meal copayments. State Sen. Ceci Maher, chair of the Senate Committee on Children, praised the move but urged lawmakers to go further.

item.description: Editorial cartoons by Dave Whamond & John Darkow

item.title: Tong: CT Issued Dozens Of Warnings Of Data Privacy Act In 2025
item.description: Key changes highlighted in the report include stronger protections for minors’ data, broader definition of sensitive data, and new disclosure requirements related to artificial intelligence.

item.title: Lamont Outlines Plan To Provide Universal Free Breakfast, Expand Free Lunch To CT Students
item.description: The FY2027 budget proposal that Lamont presented to the Connecticut General Assembly at the opening of the legislative session on Wednesday includes $12 million in funding to provide free breakfast to all of the state’s K-12 public school students, and also includes $500,000 to eliminate all fees for those who qualify for reduced-price lunches.

item.title: CT Creates $330M Fund To Respond To Potential Federal Cuts To State Programs
item.description: Majority Leader Jason Rojas of East Hartford acknowledged that the fund had been established to allow the state to react while the legislature was not in session — and had included specific language expiring when the General Assembly reconvened. He said though that the ability to respond to federal actions quickly was paramount.

item.title: Connecticut’s Small Towns Press Lawmakers For Relief At COST’s Annual Meeting
item.description: At the Connecticut Council of Small Towns’ annual Town Meeting last week, municipal leaders from across the state delivered a blunt message: the cost of running local government is rising faster than small towns can sustain.
